speaker_role: current high school/college counselor (Alicia Oglesby, ~9 years as school/college counselor and director of college counseling), hosted by College Essay Guy (Ethan)
commercial_incentive: yes - College Essay Guy promotes its own paid (pay-what-you-can) courses, webinars, and resource hub throughout, though the counselor's advice itself is not a direct sales pitch
key_insights: The counselor frames the application process as colleges building a freshman class aligned with institutional mission/vision, not a personal judgment of the student's worth
She recommends parents ask students to research schools they've never heard of, noting many students end up loving colleges they initially had no interest in
She advises using a school's Common Data Set and consulting the high school counselor to determine how much a college's admissions weigh demonstrated interest

Students should own the application process (writing their own essay, being primary contact with counselors and colleges), while parents handle logistics, organization, and calendar tracking - described via a 'passenger seat' analogy

She frames deferrals/denials as often driven by unpredictable 'institutional priorities' (she cites an anecdote about a school admitting more international students one year specifically to reduce parking demand) rather than being a personal reflection of the student
For financial planning, she recommends using a college's net price calculator to estimate real cost rather than relying on sticker price alone

For the worst-case admissions outcome, she suggests a mental exercise: imagine getting rejected everywhere, rate your surprise 1-10, and use that to identify whether your list needs more 'likely' schools
specific_numbers_or_facts: Over 2,000 four-year institutions exist in the US, per the counselor
Many colleges continued extending test-optional policies year over year following pandemic-related test-access disruptions, per the counselor (specific dates/schools not given)

Referenced third-party resource: Mark Salisbury's 'Tuition Fit' platform, described as holding roughly 15,000 real award letters that families can compare against by GPA/test scores/estimated family contribution
notable_or_distinctive: The parking-lot anecdote (a college reportedly boosting international admits one year specifically to reduce parking demand, since international students often lack cars) is a vivid, non-generic illustration of unpredictable institutional priorities behind admissions decisions.
reliability_notes: Very long (65-min) live webinar transcript with informal, conversational structure and some cross-talk; specific figures (test-optional trends, institutional-priority anecdote) are the counselor's personal recollection without citation, and the college essay guy branding/course promotion is interspersed throughout.
